title: Permissions Reconciliation Daemon: backfill historical usage views after RBAC changes
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: When role/entitlement changes are applied (grant, revoke, attribute updates) we currently rely on eventual enforcement at query-time. This means historical usage aggregates, exports and dashboards may still include rows that are no longer permitted for some tenants or roles, causing compliance concerns for audits and customer requests. Goal: Implement a lightweight, idempotent Permissions Reconciliation Daemon (PRD) that consumes permission-change events and incrementally backfills or masks affected historical usage projections so that exported views and compliance reports reflect the effective permissions at query-time or as-of a requested timestamp.

Scope:
- A standalone service in the analytics plane that reads from the existing entitlement-change stream (kafka topic: entitlements.changes.v2) and cross-references with our usage event store (clickhouse/day-partitioned S3) to emit correction records.
- Support two modes: incremental reconciliation (streaming small deltas) and windowed backfill (for large role restructures).
- Produce corrective deltas as masking directives (mask_row, redact_user_id, set_tenant_visibility=none) written to the analytics-corrections topic for the query gateway and export pipeline to apply.

Progress so far:
- Spike completed (2025-03-01): validated performance characteristics of scanning ClickHouse 30-day partitions using tenant ID + event_time index — average scan of 1M rows ~ 12s when parallelized. Notes in design doc.
- Design doc drafted: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Permissions+Reconciliation+Daemon (link to working draft).
- Prototype consumer implemented and tested locally with a 100k event sample stored in dev ClickHouse. Branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/analytics-reconciler/pull/12
- Integration tests: smoke test with analytics gateway applying corrections via feature-flagged path (feature: reconciliation-applier). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/analytics-gateway/pull/7890

Trade-offs and decisions:
- We intentionally emit corrections as idempotent directives instead of mutating primary event data to keep original telemetry immutable and auditable. This simplifies rollbacks but requires the query path to understand and apply corrections.
- Option considered: rewriting historical materialized views. Rejected due to cost and long recompute windows for large customers.
- Chosen compromise: apply masking at read-time for dashboard/exports; provide a scheduled materialized re-aggregation job for customers who request a full re-materialization (heavy path, opt-in).

Operational concerns:
- Backfill windows must be throttled to avoid IO storms on ClickHouse and S3. Implement token-bucket per-customer and a global concurrency cap.
- Audit trail: every correction message contains source_entitlement_change_id, reconciler_run_id, and checksum. Corrections are retained for 180 days.

Next steps:
- Finish schema for analytics-corrections topic and publish to schema registry (owner: infra-data).
- Implement per-tenant rate-limiter and safe-guard for "org-wide role purge" events (require a manual confirmation workflow via Console for runs > 10M rows).
- End-to-end test with staging dataset and validation dashboard showing before/after exports.

Related incidents and rationale:
- Incident INC-2025-01: customer A requested deletion of a service account and flagged historical exports that still contained artifacts; manual process took 3 days. This ticket aims to automate those corrective tasks and reduce MTTR.

Design artifacts and links:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Permissions+Reconciliation+Daemon
- Spike notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-spike-reconciler
